Position: Part Time Floor Leader 
 Weekly: 20-29 hours 
 Interview Plan 
 Floor Leader 
 As a Floor Leader, you'll play a vital role in supporting the Store Management Team across all areas of the business. This includes everything from driving sales and opening/closing the store to analyzing sales results and leading training sessions. Together with your fellow leaders, you'll work to ensure that every aspect of the store is firing on all cylinders, creating an exceptional customer experience, a happy and motivated staff, and operational excellence that would make even the most detail-oriented among us proud. 
 Your day-to-day will be spent on the shop floor, where you'll lead and inspire a team of sales associates to achieve and surpass their goals. By fostering a culture of passion and positivity, you'll help create a work environment that's both productive and fun, resulting in happy customers and happy employees. The Floor Leader role is all about making the world a better place one soap at a time! 
 Responsibilities: 
 Sales & Customer Experience: 
 Driving Sales: Utilize the StoreForce dashboard results to provide effective coaching and feedback to the sales team, and make necessary adjustments to the shop floor structure to meet and exceed sales goals. Take ownership for your results and actively work to grow the contribution of your segments to the store’s overall sales. Celebrate sales achievements with your team! 
 Customer Experience: Lead by example in delivering a world-class customer experience on the shop floor, including product demonstrations. Observe and listen to consultations, collaborate with your team, and strive to exceed daily sales goals. By fostering a culture of excellence in customer service, you'll drive sales, create a loyal customer base, and build a positive reputation for your store. 
 Building the Brand: Educate customers on Lush brand values, and articulate our position on Fighting Animal Testing, Freshest Cosmetics, Ethical Buying, 100% Vegetarian, Handmade, and Naked Packaging in the shop and through community engagement, hosting store parties, and other traffic-driving initiatives. 
 Product Passion: increase the depth of your product knowledge through constant learning and consistently make informed product recommendations for every need. 
 Team Involvement: 
 Development: Train and coach Sales Ambassadors and peers on effective sales techniques and product knowledge to improve their performance, support the growth of your team, and to increase sales. Lead by example, take ownership of your development, assess your performance, and actively seek feedback, resources, and opportunities to improve and elevate your skills, knowledge and abilities. 
 Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging: Encourage open communication and actively listen to team members perspectives related to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB). Foster a sense of belonging by promoting teamwork, encouraging collaboration, and recognizing and valuing each employee's unique contributions. 
 Operational Excellence: 
 Cash Handling and Store Opening/Closing: Manage cash handling, including customer transactions, opening/closing the register, reconciling cash drawers, preparing nightly deposits, and securing the store at the end of each day. As required at your store location, take deposits to the bank. 
 Time and Attendance: Lead by example in terms of attendance and punctuality, and encourage the same from all employees. Monitor employee breaks to ensure they are taking their scheduled breaks, promoting a healthy work environment and improving employee wellbeing. Review daily communications, including store updates and task lists, to ensure that team members are informed and prepared for their shifts, promoting a culture of preparedness and organization. 
 Visuals and Merchandising: Maintain a clean, organized, and visually appealing store to enhance the customer's shopping experience and drive sales. 
 Stock and Inventory: Train your team on inventory best practices and fresh standards, and support management with inventory tasks. Utilize Visual Merchandising guidelines to make real-time adjustments to product displays based on sales and improve the customer experience. 
 Policies and Procedures: Support your management team to keep your store compliant and ensure your staff are practicing company standards for opening and closing, product integrity, respectful workplace, and health and safety. 
 Qualifications: 
 Required: 
 Minimum 1 year of experience in: 
 customer service and sales 
 cash handling and opening/closing procedures 
 supervisory experience involving coaching, feedback, and training 
 problem-solving issues related to customer service in day-to-day operations 
 a fast-paced team environment 
 Knowledge and passion for skincare, natural beauty, and ethical business 
 Flexible schedule to accommodate store needs, including evenings, weekends, and holidays 
 Preferred: 
 Experience with consultation-based customer service models 
 Experience analyzing sales metrics 
 Experience working in skincare or cosmetics 
 Experience in cross cultural collaboration and DEIB or social justice training 
 Fluency in Spanish, French or other languages

 Location: Vancouver - Hybrid  
 Welcome to GAIN! 
 GAIN is a creative-led, insight-driven company that blends data, tech, and creativity. We believe the best ideas emerge where intelligence and creativity unite, where insight sparks imagination, and where innovation turns possibility into progress.   
We are explorers of new frontiers, shaping bold strategies that move people, brands, and businesses forward. Individually and together, our specialist teams provide the vision, data, and confidence brands and organizations need to make braver, more impactful decisions.  
Today as GAIN, we work as a united force, using data to fuel creativity, and technology to unlock new possibilities. As imagineers, we don’t just embrace innovation – we engineer it; transforming information into action, and ideas into breakthroughs.    
 This is where rebel thinking, smart technology, and data-driven creativity shape the future. 
 The Role
 As an Experimentation Consultant, you own the day-to-day experimentation program for your clients. You find where they are losing revenue, decide what to test, and turn results into recommendations they act on. 
 Externally, you will lead some accounts on your own and support the Sr. Experimentation Consultant on enterprise accounts within their portfolio. On every account, you are responsible for the execution and delivery of work for clients. You will be responsible for overall client success and satisfaction through proactive client communication, relationship management, expectation setting, and positive experiment and program results, by executing research, hypothesis ideation, prioritization, strategy, and analysis. You will be counted on to manage ongoing experimentation programs, including crafting and presenting intriguing stories and actionable recommendations through data and insights from experiments. 
 Internally, you will report to a Sr. Experimentation Consultant, who manages and coaches you. You will work with the account team, including Digital Programs, to deliver value to the client while maintaining profitability through internal innovation. 
 Responsibilities 
 Experimentation Strategy & Technical Expertise  
 Overall client success, satisfaction, and retention through positive Experimentation results.  
 Research & interpret data, run statistical calculation, draw conclusions, and pitch actionable strategies, results, and insights to a wide variety of client stakeholders and senior management.  
 In-depth technical understanding of Experimentation in order to create technically feasible experiments.  
 Present insights & results with engaging storytelling to executive stakeholders (remotely & in-person) in order to secure their assurance in Conversion.  
 Develop and plan experimentation roadmaps by analyzing large and detailed data sets in order to identify the biggest areas for improvement and implement strategies to capitalize on these opportunities.  
 Maintain an advanced understanding of conversion drivers including user research, data analytics, neuro-marketing, persuasion principles, and business context.  
 Account & Client Relationship Management  
 Maintain & continually increase understanding of the client’s organizational goals for Experimentation within each engagement.  
 Working with Digital Programs team and Sr. Experimentation Consultant to build personal relationships with clients, becoming trusted partners in order to secure our expertise in all client needs.  
 Collaborating with Digital Programs and Sr. Experimentation Consultant in the planning and development of Executive Business Reviews, Insights, and Results.  
 Manage stakeholder relationships, review and obtain input at key stages, and make judgment calls on input to ensure continued alignment and transparency.  
 Help identify growth and expansion opportunities within client engagements.  
 Support the Digital Programs team and Sr Experimentation Consultant drive the account direction to ultimately ensure client success and account stability. 
 2+ years in experimentation, CRO, digital analytics or a strategy role where you owned analysis and recommendations end to end.  
 Hands-on experience analyzing A/B test results. You can explain significance, sample size and why a result might not be trustworthy. 
 Experience pulling and interpreting data in at least one analytics platform (such as GA4, Adobe Analytics or Amplitude) and one behavioural tool (such as Contentsquare, Clarity or Hotjar). 
 Clear, confident written and spoken communication with stakeholders at every level. 
 A track record of owning your work: you estimate your time well, check your own output and raise problems early. 
 Judgement. You form a point of view, back it with evidence and make good calls. 
 Curiosity. When a result moves, you want to know why, and you go and check. 
 You take feedback well. You act on it the first time and you're comfortable being wrong. 
 You can work without a playbook. You make progress when the path isn't clear. 
 You think commercially. You think about the client's business, not just the test. 
 Nice to have
 Working knowledge of HTML, CSS and JavaScript for scoping what a test can do. 
 Ecommerce or UX experience. 
 User research or survey experience. 
 Agency experience across several clients at once. 
 A degree in business, marketing, statistics or a related field, or equivalent experience. 
 How You'll Work
 Rebel Thinking: We don’t accept “good enough”. Rebel Thinking is about curiosity with courage. We make it safe to question assumptions, challenge the obvious, and explore smarter, braver ways forward, even when it feels uncomfortable. This is how new ideas, better products, and real breakthroughs happen.  
 Make It Happen: “We turn intent into momentum.” Making it Happen is about turning ambition in to action. We move fast, learn fast, and push through obstacles together. Progress beats perfection, and momentum creates impact.   
 Swarming Our Expertise: “Individually smart. Collectively unstoppable.” Swarming our Expertise means we win together. We commit to developing our expertise so that by combining diverse skills, perspectives, and experiences, we solve harder problems faster and deliver results no single expert could achieve together.  
 Hybrid work environment + a home office allowance 
 Flex-Fridays! Friday is your uninterrupted day to wrap up the work week or sign off early 
 3 weeks of paid time off to start, plus a winter holiday office closure.  
 Work from anywhere in the world up to 20 business days or 4 weeks per year! We want you to build a life and a career at the same time. 
 Wellness time, health + dental coverage, health spending account, and wellness spending account so that you can prioritize YOU. 
 Dog friendly office, because our furry friends are part of the team too. 
 Office gym membership  
 Reward + recognition programs to recognize your team (and be recognized) for all that we do 
 The typical hiring range for this role is $82,000 - $90,000 annually. This range reflects our commitment to our compensation philosophy, internal equity, and comes with a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package. Base pay will be determined based on role-related skills, knowledge, and experience.

 The Purchase team sits within GitLab's Monetization section and owns the end-to-end purchase experience for all GitLab products, including new purchases, add-ons, upgrades, and self-service promotional discounts.  Unifying separate purchase flows into one consistent purchase experience
 Building and scaling GitLab Flex subscription flows that let customers reserve spend month to month across seats, artificial intelligence (AI) credits, Runners, and other GitLab capabilities without renegotiating their contract
 Evolving self-service promotional discounts for existing and prospective customers
 Modernizing the purchase frontend to improve clarity, accessibility, and conversion
 Strengthening integrations between the purchase flow and downstream billing and CRM systems for accuracy and resilience

 Design and build fullstack features across the purchase journey.
 Lead technical design for new purchasing capabilities and the unified purchase experience.
 Partner with Product and Design to turn purchasing requirements into resilient, well-tested technical solutions.
 Ensure purchase flows integrate correctly and safely with downstream billing and CRM systems.
 Set and uphold engineering standards for code quality, testing, rollout safety, and monitoring.

 Identify and reduce technical debt and architectural risk in the purchase experience.

 Organization 
 Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is a registered, charitable organization that provides integrated, accessible, and equitable community-based primary care, wellness services, and health education to Durham community members who face multiple barriers to their health and well-being.
 DCHC also provides equity-based programs and services that focus on priority populations such as Indigenous, Black, the 2SLGBTQI Community, Newcomers to Canada, Seniors, and Unattached patients (i.e., those without a family doctor), to name a few. DCHC ensures Durham community members receive not only sick care, but preventive care as well.
 At DCHC, we are a team-based interprofessional group of staff including physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, counselors, dietitians, outreach workers, medical secretaries, and other administrative staff. We always place every client at the centre of our approach to care, based on their needs. We address these needs through integrated clinical and wellness care and health education.
 It's an exciting time to be joining DCHC, while we are embarking on an energizing path with a focus on making our biggest impact yet on local health care by diversifying, expanding, and leveraging our Strategic Plan, Theory of Change, Brand, Client Stories and Resources.
 DCHC’s 2023 – 2026 Strategic Goals 
 Drive Program and Service Integration and Client Experience Across All that DCHC Does
 Evolve Program Offerings to Improve Health Equity and Meet the Needs of DCHC’s Priority Populations
 Establish DCHC as a System Advocate and Champion for Equity
 Enhance DCHC’s Brand and Awareness Across Durham Region
 Become an Employer of Choice with a Focus on Recruitment, Retention, and Development
 Position Overview 
 The Physician will provide comprehensive primary health care that emphasizes accessibility, health promotion, illness- prevention and continuity-of-care for clients with complex physical and mental health needs.  The Physician recognizes that the primary factors that shape the health of our clients are not medical treatments or lifestyle choices but rather the living conditions that our clients experience – the social determinants of health .
 In addition to alignment with the principles and guidelines of practice and duties of physicians under the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) and the College of Family Physicians of Ontario (CFPO), the Physician will also be an effective, collaborative member of the Durham CHC’s collaborative, inter-professional team structure, providing clinical services to marginalised and at-risk members of the communities Durham CHC serves.  The Physician will demonstrate leadership skills to champion and support goals that align with and achieve Durham CHC’s Strategy, Vision, Mission and Values, internally and externally. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Provide client-centred primary care to individuals and families in a non-judgemental manner, recognizing the social determinants of health and associated health risks – taking the stance of a health advocate.
 Perform assessment, screening, diagnosis, health education/counselling and appropriate, comprehensive treatment – within full scope of practice as defined by the College of Family Physicians of Canada (CFPC) and The College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO).
 Provide medical services that address the biopsychosocial needs of clients, including clients with multiple comorbid health conditions, mental health diagnoses and/or concurrent disorders involving substance use/abuse.
 Ensure patient care and caseload is managed to achieve the goals of Durham CHC’s Multi-Sector Service Accountability Agreement (MSAA) indicator targets and with the Central-East Local Health Integration Network (CE-LHIN).
 Participate in the development and implementation of telemedicine through the suite of services available through the Ontario Telemedicine Network (OTN) – communicating with clients, connecting with peers and specialists.
 Actively participate, seek and provide consultation within an interdisciplinary model of care which includes – among others – fellow physicians, Nurse Practitioners, Registered Nurses and Therapists practicing from both Social Work and Psychotherapy framework.
 Actively participate, seek and provide consultation with external health service providers in the client’s circle-of-care.
 Adhere to and promote evidence-based practices and standards of best-practice.

Position Summary 
 We're looking for a Tax Manager to own tax for the companies Ventures builds. You'll set each new company up correctly from the start, keep it compliant as it grows, and build the process every future venture follows. The work centres on Canada and the U.S., with filings elsewhere coordinated through local advisors as ventures enter new markets. The role is based in Montreal.
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You're responsible for the quality of the result.
 Values
 Sound judgment and attention to detail.
 Taking responsibility and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how a young company makes money and how tax follows it.
 Curiosity and a willingness to change an approach that isn't working.
 The honesty to say when a position isn't defensible, including your own.
 What you'll do
 Set up each new venture correctly 
 When Ventures decides to build a company, you'll work out what tax needs to be in place before it takes its first customer: structuring input, registrations, elections, and how its products and pricing are taxed. You'll work with the founder in residence, Valsoft's finance and legal teams, and the VP, Tax on structuring decisions.
 A venture that starts with the wrong registrations or an untested sales tax position carries that into every invoice. You'll make those calls early, document the positions you take, and build a setup checklist so each new venture starts faster than the last.
 Run compliance across the ventures 
 You'll manage Canadian federal and provincial corporate income tax returns and U.S. federal and state income and franchise tax returns for each venture, reviewing what external providers prepare. You'll keep a tax calendar, records, and audit files for every company, and resolve notices and correspondence from the CRA, Revenu Québec, the IRS, and state authorities.
 As ventures enter other markets, you'll coordinate corporate and indirect tax filings with local advisors and decide when a venture needs its own registrations there.
 Own sales and indirect tax 
 You'll own U.S. sales and use tax for the ventures: nexus monitoring, registrations, taxability analysis, filing, and remittance. In Canada you'll manage GST/HST and QST, including registrations, returns, and input tax credit and input tax refund recovery.
 You'll work with each venture's finance and billing setup so customer invoices charge the right tax in each jurisdiction, and keep exemption certificates and supporting documentation ready for audit. Early customers often come through Valsoft's portfolio businesses, so a wrong tax charge lands on a relationship the venture depends on.
 Handle intercompany and group reporting 
 Ventures run on Valsoft's capital, infrastructure, and support, which means intercompany arrangements from the first day. You'll set up and document those arrangements, coordinate transfer pricing documentation with external advisors in line with CRA, IRS, and OECD guidelines, and support any inquiries.
 You'll prepare tax provisions under IFRS, including current and deferred tax and uncertain tax positions, and give Valsoft's corporate tax team its group inputs: T106 and T1134 foreign reporting, associated corporation schedules, country-by-country reporting, and Pillar Two data.
 Build the tax process Ventures runs on 
 You'll design the processes, controls, and tools that let tax keep up as the number of ventures grows, and decide where a tax engine or automation is worth adding. Founders, finance, and legal will treat you as their main contact on tax, and you'll explain requirements in plain terms.
 You'll give tax input on new products, pricing models, market entry, and partnership arrangements, summarize legislative changes that affect the ventures, and support the VP, Tax on structuring as a venture grows into an independent business.
 What you'll bring
 A CPA designation (Canada or U.S.).
 At least 4 years of post-designation tax experience in public accounting or a corporate tax environment, with exposure to both Canadian and U.S. tax.
 Working knowledge of transfer pricing, international tax, and tax accounting under IFRS.
 You can look at a new business model and work out what tax it triggers before it launches.
 You prepare, review, and file returns yourself.
 You manage external advisors and hold them to deadlines and quality.
 You can give a founder a clear tax answer they can act on the same day.
 You use AI to research, draft, and analyze, and you check the output before it goes anywhere.
 You work independently and keep several companies' calendars moving at once.
 You finish what you start and keep records an auditor can follow.
 Useful experience
 Hands-on U.S. sales and use tax compliance
 Canadian GST/HST and QST compliance
 Tax for startups or newly formed entities
 Sales tax treatment of software and SaaS
 Voluntary disclosures
 Working in a group with many subsidiaries
 Bilingual
 Who will enjoy this role
 You like getting something right before it becomes a problem. A founder mentions a new pricing model on Monday, and by Wednesday you've worked out where it creates nexus and what the invoice needs to say.
 In one week you might register a new entity, review a U.S. state return for an older venture, and walk a founder in residence through what QST means for their first Quebec customer.
 The hard part is that every venture is different and none of them waits for tax. Founders move fast, priorities shift when a venture changes direction, and you'll often set up a company whose product isn't finished yet.

 Sommaire du poste 
 Nous cherchons une personne gestionnaire en fiscalité pour prendre en charge la fiscalité des entreprises que bâtit Ventures. Vous mettrez chaque nouvelle entreprise sur pied correctement dès le départ, veillerez à sa conformité à mesure qu'elle grandit et bâtirez le processus que suivra chaque future entreprise. Le travail porte surtout sur le Canada et les États-Unis. Les déclarations ailleurs sont coordonnées avec des conseillers locaux à mesure que les entreprises entrent dans de nouveaux marchés. Le poste est basé à Montréal.
 L'IA devrait faire partie de votre façon de travailler. Servez-vous-en pour faire de la recherche, rédiger, analyser et automatiser. Vous êtes responsable de la qualité du résultat.
 Ce qui compte pour nous
 Un bon jugement et le souci du détail.
 Prendre ses responsabilités et terminer le travail sans qu'on ait à relancer.
 Comprendre comment une jeune entreprise gagne de l'argent et comment la fiscalité en découle.
 La curiosité et la volonté de changer une approche qui ne fonctionne pas.
 L'honnêteté de dire quand une position n'est pas défendable, y compris la vôtre.
 Ce que vous ferez
 Mettre chaque nouvelle entreprise sur pied correctement 
 Quand Ventures décide de bâtir une entreprise, vous déterminez ce qui doit être en place sur le plan fiscal avant qu'elle serve son premier client : conseils sur la structure, inscriptions, choix fiscaux et traitement fiscal de ses produits et de sa tarification. Vous travaillerez avec le fondateur en résidence, les équipes Finances et Affaires juridiques de Valsoft, et le vice-président, Fiscalité sur les décisions de structure.
 Une entreprise qui démarre avec les mauvaises inscriptions ou une position non validée en matière de taxes de vente reporte l'erreur sur chaque facture. Vous prendrez ces décisions tôt, documenterez les positions retenues et bâtirez une liste de contrôle de démarrage pour que chaque nouvelle entreprise parte plus vite que la précédente.
 Assurer la conformité de toutes les entreprises 
 Vous gérerez les déclarations de revenus fédérales et provinciales des sociétés au Canada, ainsi que les déclarations fédérales et d'États (impôt sur le revenu et franchise tax) aux États-Unis, pour chaque entreprise, en révisant ce que préparent les fournisseurs externes. Vous tiendrez un calendrier fiscal, des registres et des dossiers de vérification pour chaque société, et réglerez les avis et la correspondance de l'ARC, de Revenu Québec, de l'IRS et des autorités des États.
 À mesure que les entreprises entrent dans d'autres marchés, vous coordonnerez les déclarations d'impôt sur le revenu et de taxes indirectes avec des conseillers locaux, et déciderez à quel moment une entreprise doit s'y inscrire.
 Prendre en charge les taxes de vente et les taxes indirectes 
 Vous serez responsable de la sales and use tax américaine pour les entreprises : suivi du lien fiscal (nexus), inscriptions, analyse de l'assujettissement, production des déclarations et versements. Au Canada, vous gérerez la TPS/TVH et la TVQ, y compris les inscriptions, les déclarations ainsi que la récupération des crédits de taxe sur les intrants (CTI) et des remboursements de la taxe sur les intrants (RTI).
 Vous travaillerez avec les responsables des finances et de la facturation de chaque entreprise pour que les factures aux clients appliquent la bonne taxe dans chaque territoire, et tiendrez les certificats d'exemption et les pièces justificatives prêts pour une vérification. Les premiers clients viennent souvent des entreprises du portefeuille de Valsoft. Une erreur de taxe touche donc une relation dont l'entreprise dépend.
 Gérer l'intersociétés et la déclaration au niveau du groupe 
 Les entreprises fonctionnent avec le capital, l'infrastructure et le soutien de Valsoft, ce qui crée des ententes intersociétés dès le premier jour. Vous mettrez en place et documenterez ces ententes, coordonnerez avec des conseillers externes la documentation sur les prix de transfert conformément aux lignes directrices de l'ARC, de l'IRS et de l'OCDE, et soutiendrez l'entreprise lors des demandes de renseignements.
 Vous préparerez les provisions d'impôt selon les IFRS, y compris l'impôt exigible et différé et les positions fiscales incertaines, et fournirez à l'équipe de fiscalité corporative de Valsoft les données dont elle a besoin pour le groupe : déclarations de renseignements étrangers T106 et T1134, annexes sur les sociétés associées, déclaration pays par pays et données du Pilier Deux.
 Bâtir le processus fiscal de Ventures 
 Vous concevrez les processus, les contrôles et les outils qui permettent à la fiscalité de suivre le rythme à mesure que le nombre d'entreprises augmente, et déciderez où un moteur fiscal ou de l'automatisation en vaut la peine. Les fondateurs, les équipes Finances et Affaires juridiques vous considéreront comme leur principale personne-ressource en fiscalité, et vous leur expliquerez les exigences en termes simples.
 Vous donnerez votre avis fiscal sur les nouveaux produits, les modèles de tarification, l'entrée dans de nouveaux marchés et les partenariats, résumerez les changements législatifs qui touchent les entreprises, et appuierez le vice-président, Fiscalité sur la structure lorsqu'une entreprise devient une société indépendante.
 Ce que vous apportez
 Le titre de CPA (Canada ou États-Unis).
 Au moins 4 ans d'expérience en fiscalité après l'obtention du titre, en cabinet comptable ou en entreprise, touchant à la fois la fiscalité canadienne et américaine.
 Une connaissance pratique des prix de transfert, de la fiscalité internationale et de la comptabilisation des impôts selon les IFRS.
 Vous savez examiner un nouveau modèle d'affaires et déterminer ses conséquences fiscales avant son lancement.
 Vous préparez, révisez et produisez vous-même les déclarations.
 Vous gérez des conseillers externes et les tenez responsables des échéances et de la qualité.
 Vous savez donner à un fondateur une réponse fiscale claire sur laquelle il peut agir le jour même.
 Vous utilisez l'IA pour faire de la recherche, rédiger et analyser, et vous vérifiez le résultat avant qu'il aille plus loin.
 Vous travaillez de façon autonome et faites avancer les calendriers de plusieurs sociétés à la fois.
 Vous terminez ce que vous commencez et tenez des dossiers qu'un vérificateur peut suivre.
 Expérience utile
 Conformité pratique en sales and use tax américaine
 Conformité en TPS/TVH et TVQ
 Fiscalité de jeunes entreprises ou de sociétés nouvellement constituées
 Traitement des logiciels et du SaaS en matière de taxes de vente
 Divulgations volontaires
 Travail au sein d'un groupe comptant de nombreuses filiales
 Bilingue
 Qui aimera ce poste
 Vous aimez régler les choses avant qu'elles deviennent des problèmes. Un fondateur mentionne un nouveau modèle de tarification le lundi, et le mercredi, vous savez déjà où il crée un lien fiscal et ce que la facture doit indiquer.

Our Mission
Swapcard is the leading AI-powered event platform designed to drive revenue growth and foster meaningful connections at in-person and hybrid events. We recognize the importance of teamwork in successful events; that's why Swapcard is fueled by a team of innovators who are passionate about helping organizers build future-proof events.

Our Vision
At Swapcard, we believe in the power of meaningful connections.  This belief fuels our commitment to pioneering modern solutions that empower organizers to create engaging event experiences.
 Guided by our commitment to excellence and collaboration, we aim to redefine the landscape of event technology, setting new standards for engagement, accessibility, and impact.

Our Beliefs
At Swapcard, diversity is at the core of our success. With 42 nationalities represented among our 180+ team members, we champion diversity as a catalyst for creativity, collaboration, and unparalleled innovation.

We believe that by embracing a multitude of backgrounds, cultures, and viewpoints, we can truly understand and cater to the needs of our global community of event organizers and participants.
Our full remote opportunities empower our team to thrive, no matter where they are in the world, fostering a culture of flexibility and inclusion.


Swapcard is the platform behind some of the largest trade shows, conferences and association events in the world, and our Customer Account Managers own the relationship with the organisers who run them.
We're investing in the next stage of that relationship: growth. Our clients don't run one event — they run portfolios, sometimes more than a hundred events, each with its own calendar, its own team and its own decision points. Growing alongside them at that scale is a discipline in its own right: a repeatable motion, a shared qualification standard, and a rhythm built around the client's event cycle rather than our fiscal quarters.
The CAM team sits inside our Customer organisation, alongside Solution Design, Implementation and Support. Whoever leads it works shoulder to shoulder with the teams that scope, deliver and support everything the CAMs sell.
Today, two team leads run the CAM function reporting directly into leadership. As we accelerate the growth motion, we want a single senior leader to bring that work together — someone who builds the playbook with the team, coaches them on live calls, and holds a clear analytical view of where the opportunity sits. That's the role.

Scope: Portfolio. 500+ events across our installed base, run by organisers whose portfolios range from a handful of events to well over a hundred.
 Team. 10+ people spread between the US and Europe. Two CAM leads report to you directly who run the rest of the team.
 Target. +20% growth on the installed base, delivered through an account-based strategy.
 Two levers. Higher penetration of each client's event portfolio, and upsell of digital add-ons and additional modules on the events already running on Swapcard.
 Mandate. Renew, expand, and prevent churn and downsell.
Responsibilities: Lead the CAM team. You'll lead the Customer Account Manager teams across North America and EMEA through your Strategic Account Managers and Team Leads, and set the standard for the wider CAM organisation.
 Own the number. Carry the +20% growth target and build the account-based plan behind it: which accounts, which events inside their portfolio, which modules, in which order, and what has to be true for each to land.
 Protect the base. Churn and downsell are rarely a surprise to someone who is looking. Build the early-warning discipline, get ahead of the competitive and budget conversations, and treat renewal as a managed motion rather than a date on a calendar.
 Build the growth motion. Shape the qualification standard the team works to, the criteria that let an opportunity enter the forecast, and the discipline that keeps the picture current. You'll define what counts as good evidence and help the team hold to it consistently.
 Coach on live calls. Join discovery calls alongside the CAMs, debrief together afterwards, and help shape how the next conversation goes. This is where most of the value of the role sits. We expect a lot of hands-on coaching.
 Own the KPIs and the weekly rhythm. Activity, contact creation, qualification progress, outreach, forecast. You'll build the pack, read it before anyone else does, and bring attention to where it's needed early rather than explaining it late.
 Run the enablement programme. Build it, run it, and certify the team on real accounts. Enablement here is a line responsibility that sits with you, not something handed off.
 Align the system. Marketing, Revenue Ops, Sales Enablement, Solution Design and Product. An account-based motion only works when those move together, and making that happen is your job rather than someone else's favour.
 Partner with Marketing on account-based campaigns. Work as Marketing's counterpart rather than a requester — personas, account selection, sequencing against each client's event cycle, and an honest, shared read of what worked.
 Influence the roadmap. Bring structured insight from the account base back to Product: what's blocking expansion, what competitors are winning on, what the industry is moving toward. Opinions with evidence behind them, early enough to shape what gets built.
 Keep the data trustworthy. Account context, classification, CRM hygiene. A stale account brief is worth a real conversation with the team, because the whole motion depends on the data being sound.
 Escalate what matters, early. Surface what stands between a client and a decision — product, commercial terms or timing — with the evidence attached and early enough for the decision to change the outcome.
What we're looking for: A growth builder in SaaS. You've delivered growth of this order inside an existing SaaS customer base — qualification, cadence, forecast, expansion pipeline — not just managed a book of accounts well. No event industry experience needed. We can teach you the industry; we can't teach the motion.
 Account-based, in practice. You've led, structured and implemented an account-based strategy for a SaaS business, with Marketing alongside you rather than downstream of you.
 A complex seller. Long sales cycles, several business units inside the same account, top-down and bottom-up in parallel. You know how to find the blocker — budget, politics, product, timing — name it, and work it rather than wait it out.
 An account manager who became a strong coach. You've carried a portfolio yourself, and you develop people in the moment: you can hear what's missing in a discovery call and help the CAM get there themselves next time.
 A leader of distributed teams. You've managed managers and a fully distributed team across time zones, ideally between North America and Europe, and you set a standard others want to work to.
 A systems thinker with an engineer's mindset. You think in processes, inputs and feedback loops. Strong analytically, fluent in data at portfolio level (CRM, complex spreadsheets), and very organised. Evidence, not instinct, is how you make and defend a call.
 Direct. Straight to the point with your team and with clients. Comfortable in difficult customer conversations, willing to push back, and not afraid to ask the hard question early rather than discover the answer late.
 Composed under pressure. You do your best work in a fast-moving, high-stakes commercial environment, and you keep the team steady when timelines compress around clients' event dates.
 A clear, credible communicator. You report upward without being chased and you partner naturally across functions.
 Useful, not essential: experience in events, media or B2B marketplaces, where the buying unit is an event and its date sets the deadline.
 Experience: 7 to 10+ years in account management, customer success or commercial roles, including at least 3 managing managers or a distributed team.
 Language: fluent English. French is a plus, not a requirement.
